text.p: The mark softened on the crosses in Europe's afternoon trade, shedding the mild gains it made earlier in the day on healthy German industrial production data.

The mark's sentiment on the crosses was dampened slightly in afternoon trade by comments by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who said he wanted to run again for the 1998 election, traders and analysts said.
Kohl said European monetary union would be launched punctually in 1999, with Germany meeting the criteria, although that would be an "extremely difficult" task.
The comments softened the mark as they emphasised commitment to start EMU on time, while some analysts pointed out his staying on as Chancellor would also be positive for Germany, analysts said.
Stephen King, chief European economist at HSBC James Capel, said the mark eased on the Kohl's announcement to run again because the German Chancellor is seen as very pro-EMU.

Moreover, "as long as Kohl is there, even if there's delay in EMU, the chances are that it would be one that would still lead to it happening," King said. "This wouldn't be the case if you had someone who didn't have the same enthusiasm."

Mark/lira was at 992.00/50 at 1505 GMT after recovering to 994.60 earlier and following its overnight drop close to 990, its central rate in the European exchange rate mechanism. It was at 992.20/50 in late Europe on Wednesday.

The mark was well-supported for most of the day by stronger-than-expected growth in German industrial output, which increased by 1.9 percent month/month and 7.1 percent on the year, outstripping forecast rises of 0.8 and 5.8 percent.

"The good data out of Germany certainly helped. The market is now back on track thinking that German recovery is under way, although there's always a double edge to this issue in that it makes EMU look like it's more likely to go ahead," said Francis Breedon, foreign exchange economist at Lehman Brothers.
Meanwhile, the Bundesbank kept its key interest rates unchanged after its regular council meeting, as expected.
Mark/Paris was at 3.3681/86 against 3.3669/71 on Wednesday, still near its 45-month low of 3.3659 hit yesterday.
The mark also weakened against the Swiss franc, standing at 85.90/92 against 86.14/16 on Wednesday after breaking below key support at around 85.95.
